criteria.extend_compiler_head: Change runtime/platform/html.ts (another lane's file) so the compiler-owned head gains the paired script tag, and plumb the pairing through createHTML and the emitted state module. Keeps every script tag inside compiler-owned head bytes at the cost of a cross-lane file edit plus an initializer signature change.
criteria.inject_document: The HTTP server inserts exactly one `<script type="module" src="<report-selected digest URL>">` immediately before `</body>` of served text/html document responses when the selected build is paired. Fragments without a body marker, non-HTML responses, HEAD requests, and every unpaired build pass through byte-identical.
criteria.serve_bytes_only: UP18 serves the verified JS/map/table bytes and records the selected URL in the report but leaves pages untouched; page binding is deferred to a later task. Smallest change, but the UP18 done-clause that pages receive the report-selected URL stays unmet.

page_binding.instructions: How should a served page obtain the report-selected paired browser script URL, given that Can source cannot render script tags and html.ts sits outside the worker's ownership?

criteria.carry_forward: Copy each replaced digest byte into every new server generation and record its replacement time in the emitted table. Self-contained generations, but wall-clock timestamps inside content-addressed output break identical-rebuild identity, and prior-publication timestamps understate the replacement age.
criteria.durable_ledger: Keep a dist-level content-addressed store (dist/assets/<digest><ext>) plus an atomically rewritten ledger (dist/assets.json) carrying per-route replacement times. Serve-time expiry keeps routes alive while now minus replacedAt stays within seven days; builds garbage-collect expired entries under the project lock. Generations stay timestamp-free.
criteria.pin_generations: Keep superseded server generations on disk and serve retained routes from them; prune becomes age-gated. No new store, but serve-time generation discovery is needed and a scan could surface staged-but-never-current bytes.

retention.instructions: How should replaced digest URLs stay servable for at least seven days across restart, cleanup, and concurrent builds while identical rebuilds stay byte-identical?

criteria.full_reaudit: Recompute browserBuildId from the manifest files array, hash-verify every file against freshly read generation bytes, cross-check the generation manifest.json binding, re-run the full post-bundle AuditBundle (references, map pairing, table shape, canaries, forbidden operations), bind lock plus lockedInstances to the server graph, and re-read all browser inputs immediately before atomic selection.
criteria.hashes_and_lock_only: Recompute browserBuildId, hash-verify every file, and bind lock plus lockedInstances, but trust the browser build's own audit for references, maps, table shape, and canaries instead of re-running it at server build time.

verify_scope.instructions: What should the server build verify about the supplied browser manifest before publishing the paired set?

state.browser_output: One verified browser generation publishes browser/browser.js (the entry; canonical `//# sourceMappingURL=browser.js.map` trailer), browser/browser.js.map, diagnostics/table.json, and browser/manifest.json. The manifest (schemaVersion 1, kind can.browser-manifest) carries browserBuildId (SHA-256 over the can-browser-bundle-v1 domain plus the files array), entry, table, files entries of path plus sha256 plus route, toolchain, inputs, lock, and lockedInstances. Served routes have the shape /__can/assets/<sha256>.js (.js.map and .json siblings). Generation files are content-addressed and immutable, and dist/builds/<id>/manifest.json binds each file digest.
state.mandate: Can has zero external users and no backwards-compatibility obligation. UP18 pairs one verified browser bundle with a Bun server build through `canlc build --target bun --browser-manifest <file> <server-project>`. The server verifies the browser build ID, the shared locked snapshot, the asset graph, and every hash, records the exact browser build ID and digests in its own verified report, and publishes the whole matched asset set atomically; a failed rebuild preserves the prior set. You advise mechanism choice only from the supplied evidence. You cannot inspect source or run code.
state.ownership: The worker owns compiler/main.go, driver build/report/output inputs, runtime/platform/assets.ts, runtime/platform/server.ts, plus narrow asset/entry changes inside compiler/internal/emit (flagged at handoff). compiler/internal/check is effectively frozen, runtime/platform/html.ts belongs to another lane, and runtime/catalogue.ts is coordinator-owned. A mechanism that needs a new Can operation, a new catalogue entry, a checker edit, or an html.ts edit crosses an ownership boundary.
state.page_constraint: Authored script delivery is closed on two sides: project Snapshot rejects .js/.map manifest assets, and the HTML author tag allowlist admits no script tag (src attributes fit only img). Can pages are documents ending in </body></html>; action fragments carry no body marker. The served CSP already pins script-src 'self' with no inline script and no unsafe-eval, so a same-origin src-only module tag is admitted without policy change.
state.race_duty: Verification must cover exactly the bytes published: browser files can change between verification and publication, and concurrent builds race for the dist. Publication is atomic over the report plus the entire asset table, and any verification failure must leave the prior verified set intact. All builds already run under one exclusive project lock with atomic renames.
state.retention_duty: Each replaced digest URL must keep serving its exact bytes for at least seven days after replacement, across server restart, prune-style cleanup, and concurrent builds. Identical inputs must rebuild byte-identically because build identity is a content hash. A wall-clock timestamp embedded in a generation breaks that identity; mutable dist metadata such as current.json sits outside the content hash.
state.server_output: One server generation embeds the $canAssetTable JSON ({htmx, project[]}) in program/state.ts and carries asset bytes under assets/<digest>/<name>. dist/current.json selects production current atomically. The asset server answers exact table routes only, re-verifies the content digest on every serve, and applies the shared content-security-policy to each response.
